title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: No raw SQL queries are introduced. All database interactions use Django ORM methods (filter, first, getattr) with parameterized lookups. The dynamic key in the filter uses `provider_type._meta.model_name` which is a Django internal metadata value, not user-controlled input.

The SSFStreamViewSet was previously read-only (ReadOnlyModelViewSet) and now gains a DestroyModelMixin, allowing DELETE operations on Stream objects. The viewset uses `queryset = Stream.objects.all()` with no visible ownership/permission filter in the diff. If the viewset does not apply authentication, object-level permission checks, or an IsAuthenticated + IsSuperuser/IsAdmin permission class (not shown in the diff), any authenticated or unauthenticated user could delete arbitrary Stream objects by UUID — a CWE-862 (missing authorization) concern. The diff does not show any permission_classes being added to accompany the new destructive capability.

evidence.content:
class SSFStreamViewSet(
    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
    mixins.ListModelMixin,
    GenericViewSet,
):
    """SSFStream Viewset"""

    queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly set `permission_classes` on SSFStreamViewSet to require authentication and appropriate admin/ownership checks (e.g., `permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated, IsAdminUser]`). Additionally, consider filtering the queryset to streams owned by/associated with the authenticated user's providers to prevent IDOR.
